description: 8 retrieval probes for redis/hiredis — a BSD-3-licensed minimal C client library for Redis with function-pointer typedefs, typedef-struct patterns, and a printf-style command interface.

probes.query: how does hiredis parse RESP protocol replies from a network buffer incrementally
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: redisReaderGetReply (line 742) drains buffered bytes into a parsed reply object — the streaming RESP parser entry

probes.query: how does hiredis open a TCP connection to a redis server with options
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: redisConnectWithOptions (line 815) is the option-driven connection factory; redisConnect/redisConnectUnix wrap it

probes.query: how does hiredis send commands using printf-style format strings
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: redisvFormatCommand handles the %s/%b/%d/etc. format specifiers — core command-building logic

probes.query: hiredis redisReply struct with type integer string and array fields
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: typedef struct redisReply (line 120) holds parsed RESP reply data — type/integer/dval/str/elements

probes.query: hiredis redisConnect function blocking IP and port
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: redisConnect (line 885) is the simplest connection entry — blocking, IP+port

probes.query: hiredis redisAsyncContext struct for non-blocking event-loop integration
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: typedef struct redisAsyncContext (line 65) holds the async state used by adapter libraries

probes.query: hiredis redisCallbackFn function pointer typedef for async replies
probes.notes: Grammar-edge-case probe: `typedef void (redisCallbackFn)(struct redisAsyncContext*, void*, void*);` (line 44) — C function-pointer typedef with parenthesised name and a function-type return-and-params. Exercises tree-sitter-c's parsing of typedef-with-function-type syntax (distinct from a plain function declaration)

probes.query: hiredis redisCallback struct with embedded next-pointer linked-list head
probes.notes: Grammar-edge-case probe: `typedef struct redisCallback { struct redisCallback *next; ... }` (line 45) — self-referential struct typedef where the typedef name is used inside its own body. Exercises tree-sitter-c's handling of forward self-reference via the inner `struct redisCallback *` member
